item.title: Ladder 18b · Ambulāns cōgitō (true pyramids, free voices)
item.description: The participle pyramid rewritten the Ladder 5 way: every line built from the line before, one bit at a time, up to a long peak and slowly down. Five sentences: Ambulāns cōgitō · Tē lentē loquentem intellegō · Verbum ā tē dictum nōn intellegō · Tē loquente, taceō · Lēctiōne fīnītā, ambulō. Then a review, one day, and the five again. English → Latin, then the Latin twice. Free voices (Jenny + Paola).

item.title: Ladder 18 · Ambulāns cōgitō (the participle pyramid)
item.description: A pyramid in the style of Ladder 5, on 5 sentences only: Ambulāns cōgitō · Tē lentē loquentem intellegō · Verbum ā tē dictum nōn intellegō · Tē loquente, taceō · Lēctiōne fīnītā, ambulō. Slow steps, plain → new pairs, reviews, one day with your teacher, your son and your wife, and all five again at the end. English → Latin, then the Latin twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Grammar Map · All 15 patterns in one listen (the boy and the moon)
item.description: A one-off: the gist of all fifteen Latin patterns from the app's Forms > Patterns ladder, one focus pyramid each, through a small boy learning to ask about everything, and his dad. Who (quī), when, because, if, although (Quamquam domum īre voluit, tamen laetus lūsit), says that (Dīcit lūnam nōs sequī), so that, asking, the participle, the ablative absolute, cum + subjunctive, the hidden question (Scīre vult cūr lūna nōs sequātur), result, the gerund, and -ndum est. Then the whole map in one evening, and the Latin alone twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Grammar 4 · So that, so that not (ut, nē): the heist
item.description: The Grammar series, episode four: ut and nē. So that (Nocte venīmus ut nēmō nōs videat), so that not (Tacēmus nē custōs nōs audiat), and orders (Pompōnia Bassō imperat ut fūnem portet), with the new swapped verb (videt → videat, portat → portet). A small Roman gang robs a vain senator's villa for his statue of himself, made of gold. Then traps, a grand swap, an ear quiz, and the Latin alone twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Grammar 3 · All the traps: the case of the coffee
item.description: The Grammar series, episode three: all six patterns mixed, and five traps (cum = when or with; quam = which or than; quī or quem; sī, nisi or quamquam; says that, not tells to). Then the case of the coffee: Gaius the boss is the judge, and every line uses a tool you know. A grand swap, a big ear quiz, and the Latin alone twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Grammar 2 · Sentences inside sentences (quī, quem, dīcit Mārcum venīre)
item.description: The Grammar series, episode two: who and which (quī, quae, quod), the quī / quem trap, quod as which or because, and says that (dīcō, putō, sciō, spērō, negō + Mārcum venīre). Examples first, a short rule, pyramids, both tools together, an ear quiz, and the Latin alone twice. Starring Sextus, who drinks my coffee. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Grammar 1 · Link words (cum, quod, sī, quamquam)
item.description: The Grammar series, episode one: four little words that glue sentences together. When (cum, ubi, postquam), because (quod, quia), if / unless (sī, nisi), although (quamquam … tamen). Examples first, a short rule, a pyramid for each, then swap the link, an ear quiz, and the Latin alone twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Ladder 17 · Caesar et pīrātae (Caesar and the pirates)
item.description: 75 BC, a true story (Plutarch, Suetonius): pirates seize young Caesar off Miletus. Marcus writes from the pirates' island, Lucius from the harbour of Miletus, collecting the ransom Caesar himself raised from 20 to 50 talents. Poems, 'barbarians', a sworn promise. English → Latin, then the Latin twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Ladder 16 · Epistulae dē cāseō (letters about a cheese)
item.description: Ten letters between two Roman friends: Marcus in noisy Rome begs Lucius for his famous cheese; a procession, a letter carrier who smells of cheese, well-mannered robbers who send a thank-you letter, and a neighbour who guards the cheese by eating it. English → Latin, then the Latin twice. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Ladder 12 · Analysis (the analysis) · English → Latin, then Latin only
item.description: Gaius wants a perfect analysis of the new product "Speed" before Friday, but every time he consults his new calendar the deadline moves closer, until Marcus discovers the product IS the calendar, and it is too fast.

item.title: Ladder 10 · Conventus dē conventibus (the meeting about meetings) · English → Latin, then Latin only
item.description: A funny pyramid: Gaius calls a meeting to cut meetings. "I will speak briefly" (then an hour), ut + subjunctive requests that crack, nisi … loquerētur, iam domī essem, quoniam nēmō audit, ego quidem tacēbō, cum … fīnītus esset. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Ladder 8 · 50 new words + 30 hard ones · English → Latin, then Latin only
item.description: Road to 2,000, set 1: the next 50 Road words (induō, tunica, sūmō, piscis, mūrus, umbra, collum, iaceō, stēlla, scaena…) in 5 scenes (morning, kitchen, walk, a long night, evening), each word heard 6+ times, plus your 30 stickiest hell words (quoniam, ideō, quidem, quīdam, tamen, īdem, tālis…) in clear sentences. item.title: Ladder 7 · Docē mē, ut discam: pyramid 3 · English → Latin, then Latin only

item.title: Chat · Celeriter an clārē? · English → Latin, then Latin only
item.description: Too much coffee, a carrot, beautiful birds, and today's chat with ChatGPT: speak fast, or speak clearly? Quotes: Īra furor brevis est (Horace, Letters 1.2), Rem tenē, verba sequentur (Cato the Elder), Sit sermō vester: est, est; nōn, nōn (Matthew 5:37). Each line in English, then in Latin. The whole dialogue 3 times.
